method: Automated inventory read every source, evidence, pathway, profile and review record in the exact manifest candidate for this ISO.

source_refs.locator: PDF physical p.24 (printed p.24), coastal protection and infrastructure exposure mapping.

evidence.compact_statement: Source dated 2025 reports: Most settlement and infrastructure lie on narrow Bottomside; low lagoon areas in Meneng, Anibare, Ijuw and Yaren are most exposed, unlike higher west and northwest districts.
recommendations: No wording change is indicated by the record-only check; keep the claim provisional until its cited passage is independently reopened.

evidence.compact_statement: Source dated 2025 reports: CIVRA estimates 0.7% of buildings are currently exposed to inundation and 2.3% may be exposed at 0.35-m sea-level rise by 2070; it gives 0.21–0.25 m rise by 2050.

source_refs.locator: PDF physical p.21 (printed p.11), land rehabilitation and Higher Ground Initiative.

evidence.compact_statement: RONAdapt II reports that wartime explosives and jagged limestone pinnacles hamper land development because removal or rehabilitation is costly. It identifies land rehabilitation as necessary for housing, water catchment and infrastructure and describes the Higher Ground Initiative as a climate-resilient land-use program. Explosive extent and separate costs are unspecified.

pathways.compact_statement: Wartime explosive remnants and mined-land rehabilitation costs constrain the usable higher-ground land needed for planned coastal adaptation.
alternative_explanations: Phosphate-mining damage, outdated land legislation, finance and technical capacity are additional constraints; the explosives' separate contribution is not quantified.
pathways.uncertainty: Historical war legacy, not current armed conflict. No explosive inventory, clearance cost, site hazard boundary or measured relocation delay is established.
recommendations: Keep the reverse mechanism bounded to the named institution, population and place supported by its cited evidence; do not infer violence from climate vulnerability.
